title: Which volcano darkened the skies in 536
summary: The source of the eruption remains to be found. Rabaul, Krakatoa, Ilopango and Iceland have all been ruled out; ice-core ash points to several eruptions in North America.
why: The 536 event is linked to extreme weather, possibly including the fall of Teotihuacan.

notes.problem: Northern Cordilleran province is Canadian, not Alaskan.

question: Which eruption caused the volcanic winter of 536 CE?
evidence: Ice-core geochemistry distinguishes at least three synchronous North American eruptions: one linked to Mono Craters, others likely the eastern Aleutians and Northern Cordilleran province.
wouldSettle: Ash in the ice matched chemically and by date to a specific volcano.

theories.name: Multiple North American eruptions
theories.idea: Several near-simultaneous eruptions, at Mono Craters, the eastern Aleutians and the Northern Cordilleran province, caused the cooling.
